nom: The Ordinary Natural Moisturizing Factors + Beta Glucan Lightweight Gel Moisturizer

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin most often report this moisturizer controls shine and reduces breakouts without over-drying, and several call it the best option specifically for oily skin.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin largely find it insufficient on its own, describing tightness, dryness, or a residue that sits on top of dry patches rather than hydrating them, though a couple use it successfully layered under a heavier cream or oil.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers are split: several praise it for balancing oily zones while helping with clogged pores and breakouts, but others with drier or comedone-prone combination skin find it too light and either dehydrating or breakout-inducing.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers mostly report it is calming, with reduced redness and no burning, though one sensitive user experienced new redness and irritation.
segments.normal: Reviewers with normal skin describe it as not hydrating enough, leaving a tight feeling, and suggest it suits oilier skin better.
segments.mature: The one mature-skin reviewer (60+) reports strong, lasting hydration through winter with only occasional need for an added oil.

concerns.aging: A mature reviewer reports the product keeps her skin soft all day even in winter; another long-term user describes fading of old scars on the neck/chest, though this is presented as an unexpected, unverified effect.
concerns.dehydration: Reports are split by skin type: oily and normal-to-oily users say it hydrates adequately or well, while several dry-skin users say it leaves skin tight, dry, or dependent on a second heavier moisturizer layered on top.
concerns.redness: Most reviewers who mention redness say it decreased or calmed down, including rosacea and sensitive-skin users; a minority report the product itself caused new redness and irritation.
concerns.barrier: Reviewers generally describe it as sealing in other products and supporting the skin barrier without clogging pores; one reviewer specifically credits it with quick barrier repair.
concerns.spots: Several acne-prone reviewers report fewer breakouts and calmer active spots, including on hormonal acne and rosacea-related redness.
concerns.blemishes: Most acne-prone reviewers report no new breakouts and clearer skin over time; a few specifically describe new whiteheads or cystic-type breakouts after use.
concerns.oiliness: Oily-skin reviewers consistently report reduced shine and oil control through the day, with the product frequently described as keeping skin matte without drying it out.

aspects.libelle: Insufficient alone in cold or dry conditions
Layers well under makeup and other products

extraits.texte: I have combination skin, with a lot of closed comedones, so i use retinal and a BHA face wash that help me a lot, but make my skin dehydrated (which is a problem that I have anyway, those products just make it a bit worse). I bought this cream for the summer, because I wanted something light to use at the end of my routine, but this is useless, it's like not putting anything on. A lot of creams break me out, this one didn't but also leaves my skin completely dehydrated, as if i didn't use it at all. Also i don't have a lot of irritation, but this product doesn't help at all with the little that i have. I prefer the NMF + HA cream, even though it does break me out sometimes as it is too heavy for my skin, since it is prone to clogged pores.

I have combination skin (forehead can get a bit oily but i sometimes get eczema and dry patches around my nose and mouth) so because it said it targets dryness I gave it a shot - it didn't feel like it hydrated my skin at all and after application I was still bothered by the tight feeling I get after washing my face. It felt like it just put a layer over the dry parts of my face without adding anything to them. I'm sure this is a good product and would work well for someone with oily skin but I would really avoid if you need any hydration from your moisturiser. I'm switching back to the original natural moisturising factors having not used much of this.
I suffer from rosacea and very dry skin. This moisturizer helped improve my skins texture and really hydrated my skin. It bas no scent, which I prefer.

This is the best moisturizer for those with oily skin! I work in a hospital and this is the only moisturizer that has been able to keep my oil at bay to reduce breakouts without drying out my skin. It probably wouldn't work for those with normal and dry skin. I do have normal patches around my eyes so I use the Derma-E Skin Restore Advanced Peptides at night. Together, these are a dream team for those who want beautifully moisturized but not too oily skin that work in a hospital! For refernce, I have oily, acne-prone skin. I use Derma-E Acne Deep Pore Cleansing face cleanser, The Ordinary's niacinamide serum, and this moisturizer for day time plus the Derma-E moisturizer mentioned above at night time. With this combo, I have minimal acne only around where hospital masks, hairnets, etc touch.

I have oily, acne-prone skin that is also dehydrated and becomes dull and congested very easily. I have looked for decades for a gel moisturizer like this that does not contain silicones/dimethicone or fragrance, which also break me out. This is it! I never want to be without it, please never discontinue it! Not only does it provide the perfect amount of moisture for me, the beta glucan calms breakouts and redness. Truly the best ever.

extraits.titre: Dry skin people, hear me out
extraits.texte: I have dry skin and I love this. I use it in place of an essence. I always follow with a heavier moisturizer. Nothing can beat the beta glucan amount found in this moisturizer.

extraits.titre: Superb hydration even for winter mature skin
extraits.texte: I got this for the summer but am still using this in winter. It's amazingly hydrating for my 60+ skin and keeps skin soft all day. Only when it's really cold outside do I add a drop oil. Such a great buy compared with the ceramide NMF which can produce a bit of an oil slick with some squalane based serums.
